datasets.name: Cost and Usage
datasets.description: Describes the cost and usage incurred through using or purchasing a service provider's resources or services.
relationships_text: The Cost and Usage dataset can be joined to the Contract Commitment dataset through the use of the Contract Commitment ID.

* In the Cost and Usage dataset, Contract Commitment ID is a property within a JSON object array provided in Contract Applied column.
* In the Contract Commitment dataset, Contract Commitment ID is a column.

datasets.name: SKU Price
datasets.description: Describes the catalog rates, internal multipliers, and negotiated unit prices for resources or services offered by a service provider.
relationships_text: The SKU Price dataset relates to the Cost and Usage dataset through the SKU Price ID, enabling the attribution of catalog rates to incurred usage. This is a one-to-many relationship: a single SKU Price ID corresponds to multiple SKU Price records, because a SKU's price varies by effective period, contract, pricing currency, and unit price type.
Resolving the price that applies to a Cost and Usage charge therefore requires more than the SKU Price ID alone. The charge must also be aligned to the SKU Price record using the following criteria:

* Service Provider: The Cost and Usage Service Provider Name matches the SKU Price record's Service Provider Name.
* Effective Period: The Cost and Usage Charge Period Start is on or after the SKU Price record's SKU Price Effective Start and before its SKU Price Effective End; for this criterion, a null SKU Price Effective Start represents the earliest available time, and a null SKU Price Effective End represents the latest available time.
 Contract: The Contract ID matches a ContractId property extracted from the charge's Contract Applied array (ContractApplied.Elements[].ContractId), or is null for a public list price. Note that ContractApplied only resolves prices associated with contract commitments.
* Pricing Currency: The SKU price's Pricing Currency matches the charge's PricingCurrency, or the charge's BillingCurrency when the operating model does not include pricing and billing currency differences.
* Unit Price Type: The SKU Price record's Unit Price Type is filtered to a single value (e.g., "List"). Because one contract can carry more than one price type for the same SKU Price ID (e.g., a "Base" rate and a "Contracted" rate), the other criteria alone can match more than one record. Comparing a billed contracted rate against its published catalog rate, for example, requires looking up the corresponding SKU Price record where Unit Price Type is "List".
The resolved record carries the unit price for that combination.

Notes:

* Because the unit prices in the Cost and Usage dataset (i.e., List Unit Price and Contracted Unit Price) are denominated in the Billing Currency, comparing a Cost and Usage rate against a resolved SKU Price record requires currency conversion whenever the charge's Billing Currency differs from its Pricing Currency. However, the Pricing Currency unit prices (i.e., Pricing Currency List Unit Price and Pricing Currency Contracted Unit Price) are denominated in the Pricing Currency and compare directly against Unit Price without conversion.
* Because the SKU Price dataset is delivered as a point-in-time snapshot, historical charges in the Cost and Usage dataset may reference a superseded price record that is no longer included in the current catalog. Practitioners must retain historical SKU Price snapshots to reliably resolve older charges.
Additionally, the SKU Price dataset can optionally join to the Contract Commitment dataset to relate a specific contracted price to an overarching contractual agreement.

datasets.name: Invoice Detail
datasets.description: The financial record of charges as they appear on invoices provided by an invoice issuer.
relationships_text: The Invoice Detail dataset can be joined to the Cost and Usage dataset through Invoice Issuer Name, Invoice ID, and (optionally) Invoice Detail ID.
Note: One or both datasets will need to be aggregated in order to facilitate any comparison.

The timing of Invoice ID and Invoice Detail ID availability in Cost and Usage varies across data generators. Some data generators populate these values while the billing period is still open, while others do not populate them until after the billing period is closed and invoices have been issued.
For more information, see the Invoice Reconciliation supported feature.

relationships.name: Charge → SKU price
also: ChargePeriodStart is on or after SkuPriceEffectiveStart and before SkuPriceEffectiveEnd (null = open-ended)
ContractId matches ContractApplied.Elements[*].ContractId, or is null for a public list price
PricingCurrency matches the charge's PricingCurrency, or BillingCurrency
UnitPriceType is filtered to one value, e.g. 'List'
relationships.cardinality: Many to many: one SKU Price ID has a price record per effective period, contract, pricing currency and unit price type.
relationships.join_sql:
-- Resolve the public list price for each charge, using the spec's matching criteria
SELECT c.ChargePeriodStart, c.ServiceProviderName, c.SkuPriceId,
       c.ListUnitPrice, s.UnitPrice AS CatalogListPrice, s.PricingCurrency,
       s.SkuPriceEffectiveStart, s.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd
FROM CostAndUsage c
JOIN SkuPrice s
  ON s.ServiceProviderName = c.ServiceProviderName
 AND s.SkuPriceId = c.SkuPriceId
 AND s.ContractId IS NULL
 AND s.UnitPriceType = 'List'
 AND s.PricingCurrency = COALESCE(c.PricingCurrency, c.BillingCurrency)
 AND (s.SkuPriceEffectiveStart IS NULL OR c.ChargePeriodStart >= s.SkuPriceEffectiveStart)
 AND (s.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd IS NULL OR c.ChargePeriodStart < s.SkuPriceEffectiveEnd)
LIMIT 200;
relationships.stats_sql:
WITH f AS (SELECT "ServiceProviderName" AS k0, "SkuPriceId" AS k1 FROM CostAndUsage), t AS (SELECT DISTINCT "ServiceProviderName" AS k0, "SkuPriceId" AS k1 FROM SkuPrice)
SELECT count(*) AS rows_total,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.k0 IS NOT NULL AND f.k1 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_with_key,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.k0 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_matched,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f.k0 IS NOT NULL AND f.k1 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0, f.k1) END) AS keys_distinct,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.k0 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0, f.k1) END) AS keys_matched
FROM f LEFT JOIN t ON t.k0 = f.k0 AND t.k1 = f.k1

relationships.name: Charge → contract commitment
also: The key is inside a JSON array: ContractApplied.Elements[*].ContractCommitmentId
relationships.cardinality: Many to many: a charge can apply several commitments, and a commitment applies to many charges.
relationships.stats_sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT row_number() OVER () AS r, ContractApplied FROM CostAndUsage),
  e AS (SELECT c.r, x ->> '$.ContractCommitmentId' AS k0
        FROM c CROSS JOIN unnest(CAST(json_extract(c.ContractApplied, '$.Elements') AS JSON[])) AS u(x)),
  t AS (SELECT DISTINCT ContractCommitmentId AS k0 FROM ContractCommitment)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM c) AS rows_total,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM c WHERE ContractApplied IS NOT NULL) AS rows_with_key,
  (SELECT count(DISTINCT e.r) FROM e JOIN t USING (k0)) AS rows_matched,
  (SELECT count(DISTINCT k0) FROM e) AS keys_distinct,
  (SELECT count(DISTINCT k0) FROM e JOIN t USING (k0)) AS keys_matched
relationships.join_sql:
-- Unpack ContractApplied and join each element to its contract commitment
SELECT c.ChargePeriodStart, c.ChargeCategory, c.EffectiveCost,
       x ->> '$.ContractCommitmentId' AS ContractCommitmentId,
       x ->> '$.ContractCommitmentAppliedCost' AS AppliedCost,
       cc.ContractCommitmentCategory, cc.ContractCommitmentType, cc.ContractCommitmentCost
FROM CostAndUsage c
CROSS JOIN unnest(CAST(json_extract(c.ContractApplied, '$.Elements') AS JSON[])) AS u(x)
JOIN ContractCommitment cc ON cc.ContractCommitmentId = x ->> '$.ContractCommitmentId'
LIMIT 200;

relationships.name: Charge → invoice detail
also: Invoice Detail ID is optional, for record-level matching
One or both datasets need to be aggregated before comparing
Some data generators only fill Invoice ID in Cost and Usage after the billing period closes
relationships.cardinality: Many to many at invoice level; add Invoice Detail ID to match individual invoice records.
relationships.join_sql:
-- Compare each invoice's total with the Cost and Usage charges that carry its ID
WITH cu AS (SELECT InvoiceIssuerName, InvoiceId, sum(BilledCost) AS CostAndUsageBilled
            FROM CostAndUsage WHERE InvoiceId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ALL),
     inv AS (SELECT InvoiceIssuerName, InvoiceId, sum(BilledCost) AS InvoiceBilled
             FROM InvoiceDetail GROUP BY ALL)
SELECT InvoiceIssuerName, InvoiceId, InvoiceBilled, CostAndUsageBilled,
       round(InvoiceBilled - CostAndUsageBilled, 2) AS Difference
FROM inv FULL OUTER JOIN cu USING (InvoiceIssuerName, InvoiceId)
ORDER BY 1, 2;
relationships.stats_sql:
WITH f AS (SELECT "InvoiceIssuerName" AS k0, "InvoiceId" AS k1 FROM CostAndUsage), t AS (SELECT DISTINCT "InvoiceIssuerName" AS k0, "InvoiceId" AS k1 FROM InvoiceDetail)
SELECT count(*) AS rows_total,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.k0 IS NOT NULL AND f.k1 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_with_key,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.k0 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_matched,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f.k0 IS NOT NULL AND f.k1 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0, f.k1) END) AS keys_distinct,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.k0 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0, f.k1) END) AS keys_matched
FROM f LEFT JOIN t ON t.k0 = f.k0 AND t.k1 = f.k1

relationships.name: Charge → billing period
relationships.cardinality: Many to one: each charge belongs to one billing period of its invoice issuer.
relationships.join_sql:
-- Billed cost by billing period and its status (open or closed)
SELECT c.InvoiceIssuerName, c.BillingPeriodStart, bp.BillingPeriodStatus,
       round(sum(c.BilledCost), 2) AS BilledCost
FROM CostAndUsage c
JOIN BillingPeriod bp USING (InvoiceIssuerName, BillingPeriodStart)
GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1, 2;
relationships.stats_sql:
WITH f AS (SELECT "InvoiceIssuerName" AS k0, "BillingPeriodStart" AS k1 FROM CostAndUsage), t AS (SELECT DISTINCT "InvoiceIssuerName" AS k0, "BillingPeriodStart" AS k1 FROM BillingPeriod)
SELECT count(*) AS rows_total,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.k0 IS NOT NULL AND f.k1 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_with_key,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.k0 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_matched,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f.k0 IS NOT NULL AND f.k1 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0, f.k1) END) AS keys_distinct,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.k0 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0, f.k1) END) AS keys_matched
FROM f LEFT JOIN t ON t.k0 = f.k0 AND t.k1 = f.k1

relationships.name: Invoice detail → billing period
relationships.cardinality: Many to one: each invoice record belongs to one billing period of its invoice issuer.
relationships.join_sql:
-- Invoiced totals by billing period and its status
SELECT i.InvoiceIssuerName, i.BillingPeriodStart, bp.BillingPeriodStatus,
       round(sum(i.BilledCost), 2) AS InvoiceBilled
FROM InvoiceDetail i
JOIN BillingPeriod bp USING (InvoiceIssuerName, BillingPeriodStart)
GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1, 2;
relationships.stats_sql:
WITH f AS (SELECT "InvoiceIssuerName" AS k0, "BillingPeriodStart" AS k1 FROM InvoiceDetail), t AS (SELECT DISTINCT "InvoiceIssuerName" AS k0, "BillingPeriodStart" AS k1 FROM BillingPeriod)
SELECT count(*) AS rows_total,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.k0 IS NOT NULL AND f.k1 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_with_key,

  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f.k0 IS NOT NULL AND f.k1 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0, f.k1) END) AS keys_distinct,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.k0 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0, f.k1) END) AS keys_matched
FROM f LEFT JOIN t ON t.k0 = f.k0 AND t.k1 = f.k1

relationships.name: SKU price → contract commitment
also: Optional: relates a contracted price to its overarching contract
relationships.cardinality: Many to many: a contract carries many prices and may have several commitments.
relationships.join_sql:
-- Contracted prices alongside the commitments of the same contract
SELECT s.ContractId, s.SkuId, s.UnitPriceType, s.UnitPrice, s.PricingUnit,
       cc.ContractCommitmentId, cc.ContractCommitmentCategory, cc.ContractCommitmentType
FROM SkuPrice s
JOIN ContractCommitment cc ON cc.ContractId = s.ContractId
LIMIT 200;
relationships.stats_sql:
WITH f AS (SELECT "ContractId" AS k0 FROM SkuPrice), t AS (SELECT DISTINCT "ContractId" AS k0 FROM ContractCommitment)
SELECT count(*) AS rows_total,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.k0 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_with_key,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.k0 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_matched,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f.k0 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0) END) AS keys_distinct,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.k0 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0) END) AS keys_matched
FROM f LEFT JOIN t ON t.k0 = f.k0

relationships.name: Invoice record → payment currency record
relationships.cardinality: Many to one: records point to the record that carries their Payment Currency Billed Cost.
relationships.join_sql:
-- Each invoice record with the record holding its payment-currency amount
SELECT d.InvoiceId, d.InvoiceDetailId, d.BilledCost, d.BillingCurrency,
       p.InvoiceDetailId AS PaymentRecord, p.PaymentCurrency, p.PaymentCurrencyBilledCost
FROM InvoiceDetail d
JOIN InvoiceDetail p ON p.InvoiceDetailId = d.PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId
ORDER BY 1, 2;
relationships.stats_sql:
WITH f AS (SELECT "PaymentCurrencyInvoiceDetailId" AS k0 FROM InvoiceDetail), t AS (SELECT DISTINCT "InvoiceDetailId" AS k0 FROM InvoiceDetail)
SELECT count(*) AS rows_total,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.k0 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_with_key,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.k0 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_matched,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f.k0 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0) END) AS keys_distinct,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.k0 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0) END) AS keys_matched
FROM f LEFT JOIN t ON t.k0 = f.k0

relationships.name: Invoice → invoice it adjusts
also: Matches the invoice's own ID when it doesn't adjust another invoice
relationships.cardinality: Many to one: an adjusting invoice (e.g. a credit note) points to the original invoice.
relationships.join_sql:
-- Invoices that adjust an earlier invoice
SELECT DISTINCT d.InvoiceId, d.ReferenceInvoiceId, o.InvoiceIssueDate AS OriginalIssued
FROM InvoiceDetail d
JOIN InvoiceDetail o ON o.InvoiceId = d.ReferenceInvoiceId
WHERE d.ReferenceInvoiceId <> d.InvoiceId;
relationships.stats_sql:
WITH f AS (SELECT "ReferenceInvoiceId" AS k0 FROM InvoiceDetail), t AS (SELECT DISTINCT "InvoiceId" AS k0 FROM InvoiceDetail)
SELECT count(*) AS rows_total,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.k0 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_with_key,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.k0 IS NOT NULL) AS rows_matched,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f.k0 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0) END) AS keys_distinct,
  count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.k0 IS NOT NULL THEN concat_ws('|', f.k0) END) AS keys_matched
FROM f LEFT JOIN t ON t.k0 = f.k0
